sentences.text:
Alaudin Ansari @ Tetu .... .... .... Petitioner Versus
1. The State of Jharkhand
2. Rabina Bibi .... .... .... Opp. Parties

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Gautam Kumar
Choudhary

For the Petitioner : Mr. Yasir Arafat, Advocate Mr. Shahid Yunus, Advocate For the
State : Mr. P.K. Chatterjee, Special P.P. For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Lalit Yadav, Advocate

1 .  This criminal revision is preferred against the judgment of conviction and sentenced passed in Cr.
Appeal No.26 of 2016 arising out of Madhupur P.S. Case No.32 of 2012 by which the appellant has been convicted under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to R.I. for two years and fine of Rs.5000/-.
2.
Learned counsel on behalf of petitioner confines his argument on the point of sentence.
It is submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between both sides and after divorce, both of them contracted second marriage.
I.A. No.6933 of 2023 has been filed regarding averment that a joint compromise petition has been filed by both sides before the court below.

Photocopy of the joint compromise petition has been annexed with the interlocutory application as Annexure-A.
3.

In this case, notice was earlier issued on opposite party no.2 who had appeared and Vakalatnama has been filed on her behalf and therefore, the appellant cannot be acquitted of the charges on the basis of the compromise petition.

4. Considering the submissions advanced on behalf of both sides and the materials on record, the conviction of the appellant is affirmed with modification of sentence and the period already undergone will be sufficient to meet the ends of justice in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Badal Deb and Another Versus State of Assam, (2006) 10 SCC 540.
